nodes.description: The FMR1 CGG repeat is processed by an aberrant DNA mismatch-repair route: the MutSβ (MSH2-MSH3) recognition complex, with the MutLγ (MLH1-MLH3) effector complex acting downstream, is required for germline and somatic CGG expansion in knock-in mouse models of the fragile X-associated disorders. This is the CGG-class instance of the module's aberrant-MMR machinery and lies upstream of the full-mutation methylation silencing that abolishes FMRP. Unlike the CAG/CTG disorders, ongoing post-mitotic somatic expansion is not established as the rate-limiting driver of fragile X syndrome onset — in humans the premutation to full-mutation transition is predominantly a maternal-germline / early-embryonic event and the silencing is already set developmentally — so this node conforms only at the molecular MMR-processing level, not at the module's somatic post-mitotic expansion node.

evidence.reference_title: Mutsβ generates both expansions and contractions in a mouse model of the Fragile X-associated disorders.
evidence.snippet: MSH3, the MSH2-binding partner in the MutSβ complex, is required for 98% of germ line expansions and all somatic expansions in this model.

evidence.reference_title: MutLγ promotes repeat expansion in a Fragile X mouse model while EXO1 is protective.
evidence.snippet: MLH1/MLH3 (MutLγ), a protein complex that can act downstream of MutSβ in MMR, is also required for all germ line and somatic expansions.
